IGCSE Chemistry - Chapter 18: Polymers (Questions 1-8)

Question 1

(0620/42_Winter_2017_Q3) - Energy Changes And Reversible Reactions, Organic Chemistry, Polymers

The chemical equation for the complete combustion of ethanol, C₂H₅OH, is shown.

C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O

The energy released when one mole of ethanol undergoes complete combustion is 1280 kJ.

Part of the energy level diagram for this reaction is shown.

(a) Complete the energy level diagram to show the products of the reaction, the overall energy change of the reaction. [3]

Tap to reveal answer

A horizontal line should be drawn for the products (2CO₂ + 3H₂O) below the reactants' energy level. A vertical arrow should point downwards from the reactants' level to the products' level to show the exothermic energy change.

(b) What does X represent? [1]

Tap to reveal answer

X represents the activation energy (Eₐ).

(c) The chemical equation for the complete combustion of methanol, CH₃OH, is shown.

2CH₃OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 4H₂O

The equation can be represented as shown.

Use the bond energies in the table to determine the energy change, ΔH, for the complete combustion of one mole of methanol. [4]

bondbond energy in kJ/mol
C-H410
C-O360
O-H460
O=O500
C=O805

energy needed to break bonds _______________ kJ

energy released when bonds are formed _______________ kJ

energy change, ΔH, for the complete combustion of one mole of methanol _______________ kJ/mol

Tap to reveal answer

For 2 moles of CH₃OH: Bonds broken = 2 x [3(C-H) + C-O + O-H] + 3 x [O=O] = 2 x [3(410)+360+460] + 3(500) = 2 x 2050 + 1500 = 5600 kJ.

Bonds formed = 2 x [2(C=O)] + 4 x [2(O-H)] = 4 x 805 + 8 x 460 = 3220 + 3680 = 6900 kJ.

Energy change for 2 moles = 5600 - 6900 = -1300 kJ.

Energy change for one mole = -1300 ⁄ 2 = -650 kJ/mol.

(d) Dodecane is an alkane containing 12 carbon atoms. Ethanol can be manufactured from dodecane in a two-stage process.

In stage 1, each molecule of dodecane is converted into three molecules of ethene and one molecule of another hydrocarbon.

(i) Name the process which occurs in stage 1. [1]

Tap to reveal answer

Cracking.

(ii) Write a chemical equation for the reaction which occurs in stage 1. [2]

Tap to reveal answer

C₁₂H₂₆ → 3C₂H₄ + C₆H₁₄

In stage 2, ethene reacts with steam to produce ethanol.

(iii) State two conditions needed for stage 2. [2]

Tap to reveal answer

1. Phosphoric acid catalyst.

2. High temperature (e.g., 300°C) and pressure (e.g., 60-70 atm).

(iv) Name the type of reaction which occurs in stage 2. [1]

Tap to reveal answer

Addition or hydration.

(v) Suggest how to test the purity of the ethanol produced. [2]

Tap to reveal answer

You can measure its boiling point and compare it to the known data book value of 78°C. A pure substance has a sharp, fixed boiling point.

(e) Ethanol can also be manufactured by the fermentation of glucose, C₆H₁₂O₆.

(i) State two conditions needed for the fermentation of glucose. [2]

Tap to reveal answer

1. Presence of yeast.

2. Anaerobic conditions (absence of oxygen).

(ii) Complete the chemical equation for the fermentation of glucose. [2]

C₆H₁₂O₆ → .....C₂H₅OH + ..........

Tap to reveal answer

C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂

(iii) One disadvantage of fermentation is that the maximum concentration of ethanol produced is about 15%. Suggest why the concentration of ethanol produced by fermentation does not exceed 15%. [1]

Tap to reveal answer

The high concentration of ethanol kills the yeast, stopping the fermentation process.

(iv) Give one other disadvantage of manufacturing ethanol by fermentation. [1]

Tap to reveal answer

It is a very slow rate of reaction.

(v) Give one advantage, other than cost, of manufacturing ethanol by fermentation. [1]

Tap to reveal answer

It uses renewable resources (like glucose from plants).

(vi) Suggest the name of a process to obtain ethanol from a mixture of ethanol and water. [1]

Tap to reveal answer

Fractional distillation.

(f) Ethane-1,2-diol has the following structure.

(i) Write the empirical formula of ethane-1,2-diol. [1]

Tap to reveal answer

The molecular formula is C₂H₆O₂. The empirical formula is CH₃O.

(ii) Ethane-1,2-diol can undergo condensation polymerisation but cannot undergo addition polymerisation. Explain why ethane-1,2-diol cannot undergo addition polymerisation. [1]

Tap to reveal answer

It cannot undergo addition polymerisation because it has no C=C double bonds.

(iii) Ethane-1,2-diol undergoes condensation polymerisation with molecule Y. The diagrams represent the structures of ethane-1,2-diol and molecule Y. Draw the condensation polymer formed between ethane-1,2-diol and molecule Y. Show one repeat unit. Show all of the atoms and all of the bonds in the linkage. [3]

Tap to reveal answer

The structure should show at least one repeat unit with a correctly drawn, fully displayed ester link and continuation bonds.

(iv) Name the type of condensation polymer formed between ethane-1,2-diol and molecule Y. [1]

Tap to reveal answer

It is a polyester.

Question 10

(0620/41_Winter_2019_Q7) - Polymers, Energy Changes And Reversible Reactions, Atoms Combining

This question is about ethanol.

(a) Ethanol that is suitable for use as a fuel can be manufactured from sugars such as glucose, C₆H₁₂O₆, by a two-step process. Describe how this can be done. In your answer, include: an equation for the reaction in which ethanol is formed, the essential conditions for the reaction in which ethanol is formed, the name of the process used to obtain ethanol that is pure enough to use as a fuel from the reaction mixture. [5]

Tap to reveal answer

Equation: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2CO₂ + 2C₂H₅OH

Conditions (any three): Anaerobic, temperature of about 30°C, presence of yeast, aqueous glucose solution.

Process: Fractional distillation.

(b) The equation for the complete combustion of ethanol is shown. Use the bond energies in the table to calculate the energy change, in kJ/mol, for the complete combustion of ethanol. [3]

bondbond energy in kJ/mol
C-C347
C-H413
C-O358
C=O805
O-H464
O=O498

Energy needed to break bonds. _______________ kJ

Energy released when bonds are formed. _______________ kJ

Energy change for the complete combustion of ethanol. energy change = _______________ kJ/mol

Tap to reveal answer

Energy needed to break bonds = [1(C-C) + 5(C-H) + 1(C-O) + 1(O-H)] + 3(O=O) = [347 + 5x413 + 358 + 464] + 3x498 = 3234 + 1494 = 4728 kJ.

Energy released when bonds are formed = [2 x 2(C=O)] + [3 x 2(O-H)] = 4x805 + 6x464 = 3220 + 2784 = 6004 kJ.

Energy change = 4728 - 6004 = -1276 kJ/mol.

(c) Ethanol can be oxidised by hydrogen peroxide to form ethanal, CH₃CHO. A catalyst for this reaction is Fe³⁺.

(i) What is meant by the term catalyst? [2]

Tap to reveal answer

A substance that speeds up a chemical reaction but is not used up or chemically changed at the end.

(ii) The structure of ethanal is shown. Complete the dot-and-cross diagram to show the electron arrangement in a molecule of ethanal. Show outer shell electrons only. [3]

Tap to reveal answer

The diagram should correctly show 4 electrons in the double bond between C and O, all single bonds correct, and C and O each having 8 outer shell electrons, while H has 2.

(iii) The table gives the boiling points of ethanal and ethanol. In terms of attractive forces between particles, suggest why ethanal has a lower boiling point than ethanol. [1]

substanceboiling point/°C
ethanal20
ethanol78
Tap to reveal answer

The attractive forces between molecules are weaker in ethanal than in ethanol (ethanol has hydrogen bonding).

(d) Ethene gas reacts with steam to form gaseous ethanol. C₂H₄(g) + H₂O(g) ⇌ C₂H₅OH(g). The reaction can reach a position of equilibrium. The forward reaction is exothermic.

(i) State and explain the effect of increasing the pressure on the position of equilibrium. All other conditions are unchanged. [2]

Tap to reveal answer

The equilibrium moves to the right because there are fewer moles of gas on the right side.

(ii) Increasing the pressure of a gas increases its concentration. State and explain the effect of increasing the pressure on the rate of the reaction. All other conditions are unchanged. [2]

Tap to reveal answer

The reaction is faster because the particles are closer together, leading to more frequent collisions per second.

(iii) State and explain the effect of increasing the temperature on the position of equilibrium. All other conditions are unchanged. [2]

Tap to reveal answer

The equilibrium moves to the left because the forward reaction is exothermic, so the system opposes the increase in temperature by favouring the endothermic (backward) reaction.

Question 22

(0620/43_Winter_2022_Q6) - Energy Changes And Reversible Reactions, Polymers

(a) Chloroethene (CH₂=CHCl) can be manufactured from 1,2-dichloroethane (CH₂ClCH₂Cl). The equation can be represented as shown.

(i) Some bond energies are given. Use the bond energies in the table to calculate the energy change, in kJ/mol, of the reaction. [3]

bondbond energy in kJ/mol
C-C350
C=C610
C-Cl340
C-H410
H-Cl430

Calculate the energy needed to break bonds. energy = _______________ kJ

Calculate the energy released when bonds form. energy = _______________ kJ

Calculate the energy change of the reaction. energy change of the reaction = _______________ kJ/mol

Tap to reveal answer

Energy needed to break bonds (C-C and C-H) = 350 + 410 = 860. Wait, reading from answer key, calculation is based on C-C and C-Cl bonds broken and C=C and H-Cl bonds formed. Let's re-calculate. Energy needed = 1x(C-C) + 1x(C-Cl) = 350+340=690. From answer key, bonds broken = 2670. Bonds formed=2610. Let's trace from structure. Bonds broken: 1x(C-C) + 4x(C-H) + 2x(C-Cl) = 350 + 4(410) + 2(340) = 350 + 1640 + 680 = 2670kJ. Bonds formed: 1x(C=C) + 3x(C-H) + 1x(C-Cl) + 1x(H-Cl) = 610 + 3(410) + 340 + 430 = 610 + 1230 + 340 + 430 = 2610kJ. Energy change = 2670 - 2610 = +60 kJ/mol.

(ii) Deduce whether the energy change for this reaction is exothermic or endothermic. Give a reason for your answer. [1]

Tap to reveal answer

Endothermic because the overall energy change has a positive sign.
